item.title: Positive Geometry of Oriented Matroid Strata
item.description: We study the positive geometry of Grassmannians whose boundary is a union of Pl\"ucker divisors. For the full Pl\"ucker boundary the regions are closures of realization spaces of uniform oriented matroids. In rank three we show that the pair $(\mathrm{Gr}_{3,n},Z_{3,n})$ is a positive arrangement in the sense of Sturmfels and Telen for $n\le 9$ points and compute its combinatorial rank from point counts of the configuration space $\mathcal{X}_{3,n}$ over finite fields. For seven points the canonical forms of the regions span all logarithmic forms. For eight points they do not, because the M\"obius-Kantor configuration is not realizable over the reals. This determines for seven and eight… — Arne Kuhrs, Artyom Lisitsyn — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: The spectrum of codegree Tur\'an densities of 3-graphs
item.description: The \emph{minimum codegree} $\delta_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, its \emph{codegree Tur\'an density} $\gamma(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of $\delta_{k-1}(H)/|V(H)|$ over growing $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs $H$. We prove that every real number $\alpha\in[0,1)$ is the codegree Tur\'an density of an infinite family $\mathcal{F}_\alpha$ of $3$-graphs, and this family can be chosen so that $\gamma(\mathcal{F}')>\alpha$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq\mathcal{F}_\alpha$. This resolves the $3$-graph case of a conjecture… — Jun Gao, Oleg Pikhurko, Mingyuan Rong, Shumin Sun — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: The maximum number of triangles in a graph without pentagons
item.description: The generalized Tur\'an number $\ex(n,T,H)$ is the maximum number of $T$ in an $n$-vertex graph containing no $H$. Inspired by a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s on the function $\ex(n,C_5,K_3)$, Bollob\'as and Gy\H ori proposed the problem of $\ex(n,K_3,C_5)$. In this paper, we prove that $\ex(n,K_3,C_5)=(1/(3\sqrt3)+o(1))n^{3/2}$, finally solved this problem. As applications, we determine the asymptotic value of $\ex(n,\{\text{ind-}C_4,C_{5}\})$ which answers a question of Ergemlidze, Gy\H{o}ri and Methuku, and the asymptotic value of 3-uniform hypergraph without Berge short cycle which solve a conjecture of Gy\H{o}ri and Salia. — Qing Cui, Ervin Gy\H{o}ri, Chenke Zhang, Xiutao Zhu — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: On the factorization of Dirac hypergraphs
item.description: A celebrated result from the 70s due to Baranyai states that the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices decomposes into perfect matchings if $k\mid n$. We prove a minimum degree version of this result. Note that a necessary condition for a $k$-uniform hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices to admit a decomposition into perfect matchings is that $G$ is vertex-regular and $k\mid n$. We show that, if this is satisfied and, in addition, $G$ has minimum $(k-1)$-degree at least $(\frac{1}{2}+o(1))n$, then it indeed decomposes into perfect matchings. The constant $1/2$ is optimal, as below this threshold, $G$ might not even contain a single perfect matching. This settles a conjecture of Glock… — Yangyang Cheng, Stefan Glock, Andrew Lane — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Upper bound $2^{n}-1$ for chromatic number of orbit polytope of a small cover is attained for every $n\geq4$
item.description: Davis and Januszkiewicz proved that the facets of a simple $n$-polytope $P$ which is the orbit space of a small cover can be properly coloured by $2^{n}-1$ colours. The bound is sharp for $n=2$, it is not sharp for $n=3$ by the Four Color Theorem, and it was shown to be sharp for $n=4$ by the first author. We show that it is sharp for every $n\geq4$. The polytope is obtained from the dual of the cyclic polytope $C^{n}(2^{n}-1)$ by truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$. The resolution works over an arbitrary field and gives the sharp bound $(q^{n}-1)/(q-1)$ over the field with $q$ elements. More generally, every simple $n$-polytope whose facets can be properly coloured by… — Djordje Baralic, Riste Skrekovski — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: A disproof of the El-Zahar--Erd\H{o}s conjecture
item.description: El-Zahar and Erd\H{o}s asked whether every graph of bounded clique number and sufficiently large chromatic number contains two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs, each of large chromatic number, with no edge between them. We give a negative answer even for triangle-free graphs. For every integer $g \ge 4$, we show by a probabilistic argument that there exist graphs of girth at least $g$ and arbitrarily large chromatic number in which any two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs that each require at least seven colors are joined by an edge. — Chenghua Liu, Boning Meng — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Schubert positivity for filtered bundles
item.description: We characterize formal filtered nefness of a formal quotient flag on a polarized Hodge--Lefschetz module by the formal nefness of its positive-rank total quotients. Using this criterion, we prove that quotient Schubert functors preserve formal nefness and that Schubert incidence modules inherit every commuting formally filtered nef flag. As geometric and numerical consequences, we recover the positivity criteria of Fulton--Lazarsfeld and Fulton and extend the Lorentzian polynomial theorem of Lu and Zheng to derived Schubert classes of filtered bundles. In combinatorics, our framework applies to tautological flags of flag matroids on ordinary and augmented matroid Chow rings as well as on… — Enhan Li — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: The categorical graph minor conjecture and matching complexes
item.description: In the graph minor category $\mathcal G$ of Miyata, Proudfoot and Ramos, the morphisms are the ways of obtaining one connected graph from another by deleting and contracting edges. The categorical graph minor conjecture asserts that every submodule of a finitely generated $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{op}}$-module is finitely generated; it is known for graphs of bounded first Betti number. We disprove this conjecture: it fails for the module assigning to each graph the free module on its spanning trees, which is generated by one element. A quotient of this module has unbounded torsion. We prove, however, that the conjecture holds for all modules depending on a minor morphism only through the… — Jiangdong Ai, Yongtang Shi — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Hardness of algorithmic Kadison-Singer problem from approximate hypergraph colouring
item.description: In 2015, Marcus, Spielman and Srivastava published a solution of a strong form of a conjecture by Weaver implying a positive answer to the Kadison-Singer problem - an open question of interest to several fields of pure and applied mathematics. Specifically, they proved that for all $\alpha>0$ and finite lists of vectors whose Euclidean norm is at most $\sqrt\alpha$ and whose outer products sum to the identity matrix, there exists a signed sum of these outer products whose operator norm is at most $\sqrt{8\alpha}+2\alpha$. Since then, significant effort has been put into understanding the algorithmic side of the Kadison-Singer problem; that is, the task of actually finding a signing… — Danny Vagnozzi — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Large blow-ups of uniform hypergraphs
item.description: Let \(k\ge2\), let \(H\) be a fixed \(k\)-uniform hypergraph on \(h\) vertices with at least one edge, and let \(a>0\). We prove that every sufficiently large \(n\)-vertex \(k\)-uniform hypergraph with at least \(a n^h\) copies of \(H\) contains a blow-up of \(H\) with at least \(b(\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) vertices in each part, where \(b=b(H,a)>0\). The exponent of $\log n$ is best possible. This answers a question of R\"odl and Schacht and proves a conjecture of Bollob\'as, Erd\H{o}s and Simonovits from 1976. For fixed \(q\ge2\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\), it follows that every \(q\)-coloring of the \(k\)-subsets of \([n]\) contains a set of order \((\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) on which one color has… — Dhruv Mubayi — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: On some off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey problems
item.description: We give a new short proof of a theorem of Fox and He that the $3$-uniform Ramsey number $r_3(K_4^-, K_n)$ is at least $2^{\Omega(n \log n)}$. The construction exploits a new connection with a directed graph recently introduced by Brada\v{c} in his work on off-diagonal graph Ramsey numbers. Moreover, it generalizes naturally to give sharp bounds for several extensions of this problem in higher uniformity, answering questions raised by Mubayi and Suk. — Eion Mulrenin, Cosmin Pohoata — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Score-Based Diffusion for Hypergraph Signals in the t-Spectral Domain
item.description: We introduce the first score-based generative model for signals on a fixed hypergraph, formulated in the spectral domain of t-product hypergraph signal processing (t-HGSP). The naive tensor heat semigroup is ill-posed, since after palindromic symmetrization the spectral slices of the Laplacian tensor are no longer positive semidefinite. A per-mode frequency shift repairs it, yielding a forward Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion that decouples per (eigenmode, slice) pair with closed-form marginals, exact score targets, and an exactly isotropic stationary law. A lightweight slice-conditioned denoiser is trained on the resulting real spectral grid. Sampling combines its score on data-active modes… — Zhiyuan Dong, Carlos Mundo-Levano, Daniel L. Lau, Gonzalo R. Arce — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math)

item.title: Triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes
item.description: We study fractional triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes, unifying the settings of Nash-Williams' conjecture on triangle decompositions and the high-dimensional Dirac problem for Steiner triple systems. We prove that every sufficiently large two-dimensional simplicial complex with minimum degree at least $(1-d_1)n$ and maximum missing codegree at most $d_2n$ admits a fractional triangle decomposition, provided $d_1/0.21+d_2/0.27\leq 1$. As an immediate consequence, we prove the asymptotic form of Lee's high-dimensional Dirac conjecture: every sufficiently large admissible $3$-uniform hypergraph with minimum codegree at least $(3/4+\varepsilon)n$ contains a… — Michelle Delcourt, Thomas Lesgourgues, Luke Postle — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Note on polychromatic coloring of hereditary hypergraph families III
item.description: For every integer $h\ge4$ we construct a hereditary family of hypergraphs with $m_2=h$ and \[ m_3\ge 2(h-1)+2\left\lfloor\frac{h-1}{3}\right\rfloor+1 \approx \frac{8}{3}m_2. \] This improves the lower bound $m_3\ge 2m_2$ from the preceding notes for every $m_2\ge4$. We also show that the worst-case integrality gap of the weighted transversal problem over hereditary families with $m_2\le h$ is between $h-1$ and $5000h$. As a consequence, every such family admits strong $\varepsilon$-nets of size at most $5000h/\varepsilon$. — D\"om\"ot\"or P\'alv\"olgyi — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: A $(17/7-o(1))n$ Circuit Lower Bound for Binary-Encoded 3-SAT
item.description: We strengthen the elementary $n-1$ circuit lower bound for a specified binary encoding of 3-SAT to $(17/7)n-O(n\log\log n/\log n)$ gates over the full two-input Boolean basis, with unrestricted depth and sharing. For each integer $w\ge5$, we encode 3-CNF formulas with exactly $m=2^w-1$ clauses over $m$ available variables using $n=3m(w+1)$ bits. The proof embeds Boolean tests in variable identifiers while retaining $n-o(n)$ free bits, and combines weighted gate elimination with a nonlinear-gate lower bound from the tests' full algebraic degree over $\mathbb F_2$. We provide Lean proofs of the finite inequality and the asymptotic bound for arbitrary acyclic binary circuits. — Theodoros Yianni, Sahibzada Allahyar — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Odd Chromatic Number of Graph Classes: Bounds and Structural Results
item.description: A proper coloring of a graph $G$ is called an \emph{odd coloring} if, for every non-isolated vertex $v\in V(G)$, there exists a color that occurs an odd number of times in the open neighborhood of $v$. For a graph $G$, the minimum number of colors required for such a coloring is called the {\em odd chromatic number}, denoted by $\chi_{o}(G)$. The odd chromatic number has been well-studied from both combinatorial and algorithmic perspectives, and several bounds on $\chi_o(G)$ are known. In this paper, we establish tight bounds on $\chi_o(G)$ for several graph classes. In particular, we obtain the following results: 1. For every block-cactus graph $G$, we prove that $\chi_o(G) \leq \max… — Musarof Hossain, Sandeep Kumar, Vikash Tripathi, Mirza Galib Anwarul Husain Baig — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: A Polynomial-Time Best-of-Both-Worlds Algorithm for Matroid Semi-Bandit Problems
item.description: Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader (FTPL) offers a computationally attractive framework for online learning, with recent advances establishing Best-of-Both-Worlds (BOBW) guarantees for various bandit settings. For matroid semi-bandits, existing methods offering such guarantees primarily rely on Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL), which requires solving an optimization problem at each round. We establish BOBW guarantees for FTPL with Fr\'echet and Pareto distributions with a certain parameter with geometric resampling in the matroid semi-bandit problem, showing that FTPL can simultaneously achieve the minimax-optimal $O(\sqrt{mdT})$ regret in adversarial setting and a logarithmic regret in… — Botao Chen, Junya Honda — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math)

item.title: Hypergraph Ramsey Numbers via Oriented Palette Constructions
item.description: Given a family $\mathcal F$ of $k$-graphs, the Ramsey number $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(k)}$ yields either a red copy of some $F\in\mathcal F$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(k)}$. In particular, if $\mathcal F=\{F\}$, we write $r_k(F,n)$. In this paper, we use oriented palette constructions and the hypergraph container method to obtain a lower bound on $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ for special families $\mathcal F$. More precisely, we independently label lower-dimensional faces and use the palette to exclude prescribed red configurations, while a container argument controls the size of blue cliques. As a first application of our theorem… — Hanzhi Bai, Xinyu Hu, Kaidi Liu, Guanghui Wang — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
item.description: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a $3$-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code… — Sayantan Ganguly — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Hypergraph Structural Entropy-Enhanced Hierarchy-Aware Semi-Supervised Graph Classification
item.description: Semi-supervised graph classification aims to learn graph-level representations by leveraging a large number of unlabeled graphs alongside a small set of labeled ones, effectively mitigating the issue of label scarcity. Despite significant progress by various semi-supervised learning strategies, complex relationships among graph vertices beyond pairwise edges, especially hierarchical structures, remain underexplored by existing methods. In this work, we propose a Hypergraph Structural Entropy-Enhanced hierarchy-aware framework, namely HypSEE, for semi-supervised graph classification. Specifically, we first construct walk-induced and embedding-derived hypergraphs to capture hierarchy-aware… — Guangjie Zeng, Hao Peng, Angsheng Li, Li Sun, Chunyang Liu, Yicheng Pan — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math)

item.title: Algebraic matroids with non-algebraic duals exist in any positive characteristic
item.description: We show that for every field $K$ of positive characteristic there exists an algebraic matroid $M$ over $K$ such that the dual matroid $M^*$ is not algebraic over any field. Our conceptual proof relies on the theory of matroids over one-dimensional algebraic groups. As an application, we deduce that the classes of supports of realizable volume polynomials and of realizable covolume polynomials differ in positive characteristic. — Lukas Grund — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Partial flags of tropical linear spaces may not complete
item.description: We construct two valuated matroids of ranks 2 and 4 on eight elements that form a valuated quotient, such that no rank 3 valuated matroid forms a valuated quotient with both simultaneously. In other words, a partial flag of tropical linear spaces need not extend to a complete flag containing every intermediate dimension. — Christopher Eur — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: A note on Tur\'an densities of daisies and hypergraph products
item.description: The Tur\'an density of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ is defined as ${\pi}(\mathcal{H})=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{H})/\binom{n}{r}$, where $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal H)$ denotes the largest number of edges in an $\mathcal H$-free $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. For integers $r\geq s\geq2$ and $t\geq s$, an $(r,s,t)$-daisy $\mathcal D_r(s,t)$ is the $r$-uniform hypergraph consisting of all unions of a fixed $(r-s)$-set with the $s$-subsets of a disjoint $t$-set. We show that for every fixed $s\geq3$, \[ \lim_{r\rightarrow\infty}{\pi}(\mathcal D_r(s,t))=1-O_s(t^{-(s-1)}) \] as $t\rightarrow\infty$. This bound is best possible up to the implicit… — Marko Peji\'c — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Hypergraph Hajnal-Szemer\'edi
item.description: A seminal result of Hajnal and Szemer\'edi from 1970 asserts that every graph on $n$ vertices with $q\;|\;n$ and minimum degree at least $\Big(1-\frac{1}{q}\Big)n$ admits a $K_q$-factor (a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_q$ spanning all vertices). There has been sustained interest in extending this result to hypergraph $K_q^r$-factors. For general $q$ and $r$, Lu and Sz\'ekely in 2007 showed that every large enough, $r$-graph $G$ with $q\mid v(G)$ and $\delta_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1- \frac{c}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ admits a $K_q^r$-factor (where $c$ is a constant depending on $r$ but not $q$), and there have been various subsequent improvements to the constant (but not the order) of… — Michelle Delcourt, Cicely Henderson, Thomas Lesgourgues, Luke Postle — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: A very robust Ramsey theorem for hypergraph matchings
item.description: A fundamental result in Ramsey theory due to Alon, Frankl and Lov\'asz gives an exact formula for the $q$-colour Ramsey numbers of matchings in $r$-uniform hypergraphs: if $n\ge\mathsf{AFL}_r(\mathbf{t})=(r-1)\|\mathbf{t}\|_\infty+1+\sum_{j=1}^q(t_j-1)$ then in any $q$-edge-colouring of $K^r_n$ there is some colour $j$ with a matching of size $t_j$. We show that a very weak quasirandomness assumption suffices for this Ramsey property: we can replace $K^r_n$ by any $r$-graph $H$ on at least $\mathsf{AFL}_r(\mathbf{t})+o(n)$ vertices that is a sublinear connector, meaning that it has no balanced $r$-partite holes of linear size. This generalises the result for $r=2$ (ordinary graphs) that we… — Peter Keevash, Peleg Michaeli — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: New lower bounds for six small hypergraph Ramsey numbers
item.description: Let $R(k,l;t)$ denote the least $n$ such that every colouring of the $t$-subsets of an $n$-set with two colours has $k$ points all of whose $t$-subsets have the first colour, or $l$ points all of whose $t$-subsets have the second. We give explicit colourings proving $R(4,5;3)\ge 38$, $R(4,6;3)\ge 71$, $R(5,5;3)\ge 99$, $R(5,6;4)\ge 201$, $R(6,6;4)\ge 601$ and $R(6,6;5)\ge 84$. The first three improve the bounds 35, 63 and 88 listed in Radziszowski's dynamic survey. The last three improve the listed bounds 67, 133 and 72, and for the two 4-uniform numbers also the values 159 and 317 of a recent data deposit. The colourings of 3-subsets are invariant under groups of affine maps $x\mapsto… — Christian Lysenst{\o}en — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Connectivity of Matroids with Breadth-Critical Tangles
item.description: We construct an explicit infinite sequence of nonnegative integers $(s_0,s_1,\ldots)$ such that, for every $k\ge2$, every finite matroid with a breadth-critical tangle of order at least $k$ is $(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_{k-2})$-connected. The constants $s_i$ depend only on $i$. This proves a conjecture of Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple, and Whittle. — Zhuo Li, Zhen Chen — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Circuit spectra for binary matroids
item.description: The circuit spectrum of a matroid is defined to be the set of circuit sizes. The circuit $e$-spectrum of a matroid is the set of circuit sizes of the matroid containing the element $e$. The circuit spectrum problem is an important problem. Erd\H{o}s (1992) conjectured that every connected graph $G$ with girth $g$ and average degree $d$ has a cycle spectrum of size at least $\Omega(d^{\lfloor (g-1)/2 \rfloor})$. Sudakov and Verstra\"{e}te (2008) proved the full conjecture of Erd\H{o}s in a stronger form. It is natural to consider the size of the circuit spectra of binary matroids. Murty (1971) characterized all connected binary matroids with circuit spectra of size one. Lemos et al. (2011)… — Bing Wei, Haidong Wu, Shunzhe Zhang — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: An Upper Bound on the Proportional Choice Number of a Graph
item.description: Proportional choosability is a list analogue of equitable coloring introduced in 2019 that imposes both upper and lower bounds on color class sizes based on the availability of each color. The proportional choice number of a graph $G$, denoted by $\chi_{pc}(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $G$ is proportionally $k$-choosable. A recently proposed conjecture states that for any graph $G$ with at least one edge, $\chi_{pc}(G) \leq \Delta(G) + \text{col}(G) - 1$, where $\Delta(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$ and $\text{col}(G)$ is its coloring number. In this paper, we prove this conjecture using a generalization of Edmonds' matroid intersection theorem due to Aharoni and… — Kevin Grace, Jeffrey A. Mudrock — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Matroid Connectedness and Component Decomposition: Breaking the Quadratic Barrier
item.description: Deciding whether a matroid is connected and computing its connected components are two fundamental algorithmic problems in matroid theory. Since the 1970s, the best known algorithms for both problems have used $O(n^2)$ independence queries on an $n$-element ground set. Our main contribution is to break this quadratic barrier: we give a deterministic algorithm that computes all connected components of a matroid on $n$ elements with $O(n \log{n})$ independence queries. Our algorithm for component decomposition combines fundamental basis exchanges with a disjoint-set union data structure, avoiding the explicit construction of the fundamental graph. Moreover, we show that our algorithm is… — Manuel Aprile, Roberto Ronco — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: A Lower Bound for the Chromatic Number of Ball-Packing Graphs
item.description: For every odd prime power $q$, we construct a finite packing of congruent balls in dimension $d=q^2-q+1$ whose contact graph requires at least $2d$ colors. Consequently, the ball-packing chromatic number satisfies $\chiball(q^2-q+1)\ge2(q^2-q+1)$, and the same lower bound holds for congruent-ball packings. The construction starts from the complements of Hubaut's $C_{20}$ graphs and uses their Taylor extensions. We give an explicit finite-field adjacency rule for the $q^3$-vertex graph $H_q$, prove its strong regularity, determine its spectrum and projection matrix, establish $\alpha(H_q)=q$, and construct a two-distance embedding in $\R^{q(q-1)}$. Its Taylor extension $T_q$ has $2(q^3+1)$… — Dan Ismailescu, Sunwoo Lee, Terry Lee — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM
